question: NITI Aayog came into existence in 2015. On which date was it formed?
solution:
The correct answer is __**1st January**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• NITI Aayog, the National Institution for Transforming India, was formed on **1st January 2015** by the Government of India.
 
• It replaced the **Planning Commission**, which was established in 1950.
 
• The formation of NITI Aayog was part of the government's effort to better adapt to **changing economic conditions** and provide a more flexible and agile framework for planning and policy-making.
 
• It was created to serve as a **policy think tank** of the Government of India and foster cooperative federalism through structured support initiatives and mechanisms with the States.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Composition of NITI Aayog**

 
 
• Chairperson: The Prime Minister of India.
 
• Governing Council: Comprising the Chief Ministers of all the States and Lt. Governors of Union Territories.
 
• Regional Councils: Formed to address specific regional issues, chaired by the Prime Minister or his nominee.
 
• Full-time organizational framework includes a Vice-Chairperson, Members, and Chief Executive Officer (CEO).
 
 
 
• **Objectives of NITI Aayog**
 
 
• To promote cooperative federalism through well-defined support initiatives and mechanisms with the States.
 
• To foster a shared vision of national development priorities, sectors, and strategies with the active involvement of States.
 
• To design strategic and long-term policy frameworks and programs and review their progress and efficacy.
 
• To provide advice and encourage partnerships between key stakeholders and national and international like-minded think tanks, as well as educational and policy research institutions.
 
 
 
• **Key Initiatives by NITI Aayog**
 
 
• **Aspirational Districts Programme**: Aims to rapidly transform districts that have shown relatively less progress in key social areas.
 
• **Atal Innovation Mission (AIM)**: A flagship initiative to promote a culture of innovation and entrepreneurship in the country.
 
• **Digital India**: A campaign launched to ensure the Government's services are made available to citizens electronically by improving online infrastructure.
 
 
 
• **Difference from Planning Commission**
 
 
• Unlike the Planning Commission, NITI Aayog does not have the power to allocate funds to the states.
 
• NITI Aayog emphasizes on bottom-up approach rather than the top-down approach of the Planning Commission.
 
• Focuses more on fostering cooperative federalism and involving states in the planning process.
